title: The 10 Best Jump Starters
subtitle: Portable lithium and lead-acid jump starters that start a dead battery without a second car, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A jump starter is a battery pack with clamps that starts your car on its own, no second vehicle needed. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (weather sealing, a boost or override mode for fully dead batteries, a 2-year warranty, a USB power bank and a status display). One warning: 'peak amps' isn't a standardized rating, so a cheap pack claiming 4000A isn't necessarily stronger than a NOCO rated 1000A. The engine size each maker lists is a better guide. They run from about $58 for AstroAI's S8 to $300 for NOCO's GB150.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: NOCO Boost GB40 12V 1000A UltraSafe Portable Lithium Jump Starter
products.verdict: The most-reviewed jump starter here by far, with nearly 130,000 reviews: spark-proof and reverse-polarity protected clamps, up to 20 starts per charge, an IP65 housing, a 100-lumen light and a USB power bank, at 2.4 lbs.
products.best_for: Most cars and small SUVs: the glovebox standard.
products.skip_if: You have a V8 or a diesel over 3.0L; step up to the GB70.
pros: 2.4 lbs with power bank and light

products.name: NOCO Boost GB70 2000A UltraSafe Jump Starter, 12V Lithium Battery Booster
products.verdict: The GB40's bigger brother for trucks: rated for 8.0L gas and 6.0L diesel engines, up to 40 starts per charge, a 400-lumen light and the same IP65 spark-proof design.
products.skip_if: You drive a 4-cylinder car; the GB40 is enough.

products.name: S ZEVZO ET03 Car Jump Starter 4000A, for Up to 8.0L Gas and 7.0L Diesel Engines, 74Wh
products.verdict: A best-selling budget pack rated for engines as big as the GB70's for well under half the price, with a force-start button for 0-volt batteries, a 74 Wh power bank, a 500-lumen light and a 2-year warranty.
products.skip_if: You want weather sealing; no IP rating is listed.
cons: Peak amp figure isn't comparable to NOCO's

products.name: AstroAI S8 Car Battery Jump Starter 1500A, Portable 12V Lithium Jump Box
products.verdict: The cheapest pack here, rated for the same engines as the NOCO GB40 at under a pound, with a boost button for fully drained batteries, metal clamps and a 2-year warranty.
products.best_for: A GB40-class pack for about $33 less.
products.skip_if: You want weather sealing; none is listed.

products.name: GOOLOO A3 12V 3000A Portable Jump Starter with Air Compressor (JS-506)
products.verdict: A jump starter with a built-in tire inflator: set the pressure on the LED screen and it stops automatically, with five nozzles for cars, bikes and balls. Rated for 9.0L gas engines.
products.best_for: One box for dead batteries and low tires.
products.skip_if: You already own a tire inflator; a dedicated jump starter is smaller.
pros: Built-in air compressor with auto shutoff

products.name: WOLFBOX MegaVolt24 4000A Jump Starter with 65W Quick Charger, LED Display, 88.8Wh
products.verdict: A large pack with an LCD status screen, a 65 W USB-C port that recharges it in 1.3 hours with the included charger, a one-touch boost, IP64 sealing and UL testing, rated for 10-liter engines.
products.best_for: Big trucks and diesels with fast USB-C recharging.
products.skip_if: You drive a small car; it's more pack than you need.
cons: Peak amp figure isn't comparable to NOCO's

products.name: Hulkman Alpha85 Smart Portable Jump Starter, 2000A, LED Display, 74Wh Power Bank
products.verdict: The highest-rated jump starter here: a 3.3-inch screen shows status and errors, 65 W charging reaches 80% in an hour, it holds charge for up to 18 months, and it adds a 15 V 10 A DC output for tire pumps and coolers.
products.best_for: Owners who want clear status and a pack that holds its charge.
pros: Holds charge up to 18 months; 2-year warranty

products.name: NOCO Boost GB50 1500A UltraSafe Jump Starter, 12V Lithium Battery Booster
products.verdict: The middle NOCO: rated for 7.0L gas and 4.5L diesel, up to 30 starts per charge, still under 3 lbs.
products.best_for: V6 and small V8 owners who want NOCO's protection in a small pack.
products.skip_if: The GB70 is only $10 more for much bigger engines.

products.name: Clore Automotive Jump-N-Carry JNC660 1700 Peak Amp 12 Volt Jump Starter
products.verdict: The shop classic: a 22 Ah Proformer AGM battery, 46-inch heavy #2 AWG cables, a voltmeter and a 12 V outlet. Heavy, but it jumps car after car and copes well with cold.
products.best_for: Shops, tow trucks and repeated jumps in a day.
products.skip_if: You want something for the glovebox; it weighs 18 lbs.

products.name: NOCO Boost GB150 3000A UltraSafe Jump Starter, 12V Lithium, for 9.0L Gas and 7.0L Diesel
products.verdict: NOCO's heavy-duty pack for big diesels and fleets: rated for 9.0L gas and 7.0L diesel with up to 80 starts per charge, a 500-lumen light and the same IP65 spark-proof design.
products.best_for: Heavy trucks, farm equipment and fleets.
products.skip_if: You drive a car; it's $300 and 7.5 lbs.

avoid.name: AIMAPOW Portable Car Battery Jump Starter 8000A Jump Box (A20)
avoid.flag: 8000A claim from a 0.9 lb, 7,200 mAh pack
avoid.verdict: A small pack sold on a giant number. For about $13 more, the AstroAI S8 is a similar size and lists modest, believable ratings with a 2-year warranty.
reasons: It claims 8000 amps peak from a 7,200 mAh battery in a 403 g (0.9 lb) pack. NOCO's 7.5 lb GB150 is rated 3000 A. A pack a tenth the weight claiming nearly three times the current isn't a believable figure.
It says it starts 'all gas engines'. Every reputable maker on this list names a maximum engine size, because a small pack can't start every engine.
It lists 8 AWG cables, much thinner than the #2 AWG cables on the Clore JNC660, yet claims more than four times its peak current.

buyers_guide.q: How many amps do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Ignore the peak amp number: there's no standard for it, and budget brands inflate it. Use the maker's rated engine size instead. A 4-cylinder car needs a pack rated for about 4.0L gas; V8 trucks and diesels need one rated for their engine size or bigger.
Lithium packs weigh 1 to 7 lbs and double as power banks. Lead-acid (AGM) boxes like the Clore weigh 15-20 lbs but handle repeated jumps and cold weather well, which is why shops use them.

buyers_guide.q: What does boost or force-start mode do?
buyers_guide.a: Most packs won't send power unless they detect some voltage in the car's battery, as a safety feature. If the battery reads near zero, boost mode overrides that check. Use it carefully and only with the clamps on the right terminals.

buyers_guide.q: How do I keep a jump starter ready?
buyers_guide.a: Recharge it every 3 months, and after every use. Keep it out of extreme heat on the dashboard. A dead jump starter is just a paperweight.

buyers_guide.q: Is a jump starter the same as a battery charger?
buyers_guide.a: No. A jump starter gives a short burst to crank the engine; the car's alternator then charges the battery. If the battery keeps dying, test it or charge it with a proper charger.
